field_semantics.command: declared single-target checker command; syntax validated, not necessarily the literally executed command
field_semantics.exit_code: exit code of the controller gate run that covered the declared target
field_semantics.log_path: local evidence file containing that target's result (controller test log or acceptance receipt)
field_semantics.execution: optional record-level object, required when the pull request number is above 141, stating what was actually run: runner (ctrl_verify.sh, codex_task or other), command (the literally executed command), scope (workspace or single_target), exit_code (the integer exit code of that command) and evidence (the log_path or the identifier of the summary line inside the acceptance receipt); command, exit_code and log_path of the record keep describing the declared target; earlier records are neither backfilled nor guessed; reviewed public projections mark withheld host environment paths explicitly and use neutral evidence references; the original execution is kept in the local evidence store
field_semantics.production_consumer: optional record-level marker: none_library_only means the recorded module has no production caller in engine/http/mcp/apps as of the commit named in the record scope; wired means a production caller exists; an absent marker means this was not assessed
field_semantics.execution_runners: execution.runner additionally accepts the stage-8 gate scripts ctrl_verify_v43.sh and ctrl_verify_v45.sh; the runner names stated in the execution definition keep their meaning
field_semantics.supersedes: optional record-level array of withdrawn record ids that this re-verification replaces; every id must be listed in withdrawn_records with status superseded and belong to the same E task; a record carrying supersedes is bound to plan v4.5 or later; the replaced record is neither rewritten nor revived
field_semantics.completes: optional record-level array of still-valid record ids of the same E task whose evidence this new record completes (for example a re-run of a record with registered missing evidence); a record carrying completes is bound to plan v4.5 or later; the completed records stay unchanged and keep their own credit
field_semantics.note: optional record-level free-text note (for example a category or the task that will complete the record); it carries no verification credit
field_semantics.withdrawn_records: top-level list of records withdrawn from verified_subscopes because a revision changed the behavior they asserted: id, withdrawn_in_pr, clause, owner_task and status (pending_recheck, superseded or replaced_by_binding); every entry is pinned as a reviewed (id, withdrawn_in_pr, clause, owner_task, status) tuple in both checkers and a listed id never reappears in verified_subscopes
field_semantics.evidence_missing_register: top-level path and SHA-256 of the missing-evidence register, whose (record_id, field, path) entries are pinned in both checkers: an absent registered path is reported as missing, or as registered, not checked when it lies in the local evidence store and that store is not supplied; an absent path outside the register fails once its location is checked (outside out/ always, inside out/ with the local evidence store); a registered path that reappears fails unless its registered bytes and SHA-256 match (a path registered with unknown identity always fails on reappearance)
field_semantics.plan_recheck: per-record recheck marker of the plan §18.10 machine form: a record bound to the current plan carries not_affected explicitly; a record bound to an earlier plan carries rechecked_v4.5 when its task is in the v4.5 recheck union, keeps rechecked_v4.3 when it was verified against v4.1 or v4.2 and its task is outside that union but was rechecked by v4.3 (every task except E17 and E18), and otherwise keeps not_affected (explicit or absent); rechecked_v4.5 is valid only inside the v4.5 recheck union, rechecked_v4.4 is never valid because v4.4 was never bound by the index on its own, and required never passes
field_semantics.record_pins: both checkers pin the reviewed supersedes and completes pairs (new record id to old record id) and, for every historical record retained from the previous index binding, the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8) without plan_recheck; a missing, extra or rewritten pin fails; the records added by an index pull request are pinned by the next index pull request, after the merge of the adding pull request is backfilled; for reviewed public projections both checkers additionally pin the whole public record, and local evidence judgment requires the original record to match its unchanged historical digest
field_semantics.evidence_judgment: top-level key of the Python checker report, with evidence_unjudged: judged when every evidence path was judged and none failed (with --evidence-root, out/ paths are judged in the local evidence store it names, the directory holding out/, normally the primary checkout); not_performed_structure_only when --structure-only is given, which counts the absent out/ evidence paths, registered or not, in evidence_unjudged without judging them; not_performed when the check stopped before every path was judged, in particular when neither option is given and an out/ evidence path is unjudged, which fails the check (fail closed); evidence_unjudged counts the unjudged paths as they are met, so a check that stops early reports the count reached; --structure-only and --evidence-root are mutually exclusive; the Rust test judges out/ evidence paths only when the environment variable RSIA_SUPPORT_SCOPE_EVIDENCE_ROOT names that store and otherwise reports that the evidence judgment was not performed
field_semantics.evidence_missing_register_pin: both checkers pin the missing-evidence register file itself: evidence_missing_register.path must be reports/evidence-missing.json and evidence_missing_register.sha256 must equal both the reviewed register SHA-256 constant of each checker and the SHA-256 of the file, so no register entry (including an expected identity, an unknown marker or a missing window) changes without changing both checkers; the reviewed (record_id, field, path) triples stay pinned as well
field_semantics.pr_state: optional record-level pull request state: draft, open, closed or merged; merged requires a merged_sha and every other state requires merged_sha to be null; an absent pr_state asserts no state
field_semantics.merged_sha: record-level merge commit of the record's pull request, null only while that pull request is unmerged: it must equal the reviewed merge fact of the pull request in the Rust table expected_merge_for_pr (which the Python checker reads), differ from the record's own source_sha, agree across every record of the same pull request, and be neither the merge commit of another pull request nor the source_sha of a record of another pull request; a record added by an index pull request carries null until the next index pull request backfills that merge (with pr_state merged); it remains a manifest assertion whose git ancestry neither checker verifies
